false_assumption.statement: The Sentimental Gargoyle is the murderer of Prince Maranotti.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: The Gargoyle was present at the scene and had a grotesque appearance that inspired suspicion. His hostile behavior and proximity to the victim made him a natural suspect.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: It conceals the true murderer, Alfred Ferguson, who had a stronger motive and orchestrated events to implicate others.

mechanism_description: The murder of Prince Maranotti was committed by Alfred Ferguson (Lord Galonfield) in a struggle near a cliff, where the Prince was pushed or fell to his death. The complex deception involving lost diamonds and multiple identities was orchestrated by Ferguson to secure the inheritance and win Paula Trevison’s hand. The mind-reader Glyncamp manipulated events but was ultimately killed by the Nervous Physician, who acted in self-defense.

discriminating_test.design: A careful reenactment of the struggle at the cliff is arranged, with witnesses and physical evidence examined to confirm the sequence of events and identify the assailant. The presence of the Homicidal Professor as an eyewitness is crucial to verify the true cause of Prince Maranotti’s death.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: This reenactment reveals that Alfred Ferguson was the only person who could have caused the Prince’s fatal fall, disproving suspicions against others.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: The reenactment must show that only Ferguson had the opportunity and means to push the Prince from the cliff.
